system.summary: The second Höpken-Carlson code (as in hopken1740): four-digit groups seen between 1006 and 1915, a syllabary built for Swedish (i/j, u/v/w, a/å/ä, o/ö not distinguished) with word codes for names and terms (1287 storviziren = Grand Vizir, 1713 grefwen = comte, 1516 ottporten = Porte, 1511 hof = Cour, 1448 fred = paix, 1360 tractat = traité). Used here for French; a stroke over a group marks an accent or an apostrophe (1006' = d', 1251' = dé, 1500' = à).
system.notes: Key: hopken1740 key.tsv as on origin/main 54c4ecc65, frozen unchanged (key_frozen.tsv); key.tsv adds 24 values read from the Lit. A gloss (hopken1741a) and corrects two frozen single values (1504 vo, 1840 au).

prior_solution.where: None on these pages. No edition or modern decipherment found (web searches 11-12 Nov 2026). Castellane's correspondence of 1740-47 is in the French diplomatic archives (Nantes, Constantinople series); the clear originals may survive there; not checked.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 2245-2248) and the rules; AI language-model agents paged the volumes, transcribed, froze and applied the hopken1740 key, ran the held-out test, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.

solution.what: Images named by catalogue 2245-2248 fetched at 1200 px from four volumes (R0003590, R0003628, R0003635, R0003636) for contact sheets; R0003636 images 49-51 and R0003635 image 147 at full size; one at a time, 1.6 s apart, no block.
Image 49 (whole page) and image 50 (left page) transcribed in two passes; 5 disagreements settled or kept doubtful.
hopken1740 key.tsv frozen unchanged (key_frozen.tsv); key.tsv adds 24 values read from the Lit. A gloss (hopken1741a) and corrects 1504 and 1840.

Held-out test of the hopken1740 key (frozen unchanged from origin/main; built on volume I/9/21 from a Swedish gloss) against the gloss of the French Lit. A page (R0003635_00147): 222 of 282 groups (79%) give exactly the letters of the gloss at their place, 92% of the 242 groups in the key; shuffled-key control mean 33.4, maximum 51 over 200 shuffles (scripts/heldout.py). Consistency: eight values proposed from the sense of the bare letter before Lit. A was decoded all agreed with the Lit. A gloss (not frozen in a file, so not a formal test); three context values from the Castellane letter recur with the same sense in the reply.

Mechanical decryption with key.tsv read as French, every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py passes. Castellane letter: 79 of 94 words verbatim, 2 repaired, 13 guessed, 0 holes. Reply: 109 of 123 verbatim, 3 repaired, 10 guessed, 1 hole (after the review fix below). Dan's checker: clean share 0.444 (letter, 4 of 9 sentences) and 0.615 (reply, 8 of 13); it counts each context-guessed word as a hole.

Blind review by an independent AI language-model agent: 92 groups read from its own crops before opening the transcriptions (69 on images 49-50), no disagreement, and the two doubtful groups it met are the ones marked; key hash, decrypt.py and check_marks.py reproduced. Fixes made: reply M04, the change {x/ssi} on 1828 dropped (1828 = x is confirmed 5/5 in the frozen key; the text reads 'auxquels'); letter L12, the second a of 'Laria aille' marked {+a}. Letter read in part, grade B; reply read in part, grade B.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt in hopken1740 from the glossed despatch of 15/26 Jan 1740 (volume I/9/21), tested held-out on the glossed Lit. A page of volume I/9/26 and extended from it, then applied to these bare pages, which carry no decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Words read verbatim from the signs with key.tsv in the two documents worked: 79 of 94 (letter) and 109 of 123 (reply to the foot of image 50 left), 188 of 217 (scripts/check_marks.py); words with a marked repair, a context guess or a hole are not counted. The rest of the exchange (image 50 right page, 51 and 52, about 1,500 groups) is not transcribed and not counted.

texts.label: Castellane to Höpken and Carlson (cipher copy), image 49 L01-L16
texts.summary: After a general divan at the Porte, the Porte's dragoman invited Castellane on behalf of the Grand Vizier to a kind of congress next Sunday at which Monsieur de Romanzof (probably Rumyantsev, the Russian ambassador) is to be present; he asks the Swedes for their reflections before the sieur de Laria goes to the Porte's dragoman next morning at eight.
texts.note: 94 cipher words: 79 verbatim from the key (84.0%), 2 with a marked repair, 13 resting on context-guessed values, no holes. Every sentence is coherent French; the guessed values are mostly single syllables fixed by the sense, three of them also by recurrence in the reply. In 'le sieur de Laria aille' the cipher writes one a for two (marked {+a}). Checker clean share 0.444, just under 0.45, because it counts each guessed word as a hole.

reading_review.note: Read as French sentences against the translation: all four sentences hold; 13 words rest on syllable values guessed from context and are marked, and none leaves a gap in the sense. Checker share 0.444.

texts.label: Höpken and Carlson to Castellane (cipher copy), image 49 L17 to the foot of image 50 left page
texts.summary: The Swedes thank Castellane for his generous conduct toward the interests of their court, announce a visit next evening to set out their thoughts on Sweden's present interests with regard to Russia and Russia's differences with the Porte, and begin to say that in Sweden's critical situation with Russia any accommodation between the Porte and Russia is ... (breaks off at the foot of the page).
texts.note: 123 cipher words to the foot of the left page of image 50: 109 verbatim (88.6%), 3 repaired, 10 guessed, 1 hole (1515). One clear sentence. Checker clean share 0.615. The text continues on images 50 (right page), 51 and 52, not transcribed.

reading_review.note: Read as French sentences against the translation: the four sentences hold to the break at the foot of the page; one group is unread and 10 words rest on marked context values.

gaps.item: Rest of the exchange, images 50 right page, 51, 52 (about 1,500 groups)
gaps.detail: Same code; the key reads it.
From the sense only; glossed runs in I/9/25-27 should confirm or refute them.

The cipher has la-ri-a-[1409]-le; with 1409 = il it gives 'lariaille', so one a serves two words (marked {+a}), or the name is 'Lari'. The reviewer recalls a dragoman family of this name at the French embassy; not checked.

gaps.item: The 13 guessed words of the Castellane letter
gaps.detail: Dan's checker gives 0.444, just under its 0.45 line, because each [?word] counts as a hole; the reviewer reads all four sentences as holding and grades the letter read in part (B). If the line is held strictly, 'decoded, not read' is the fallback the reviewer names but does not recommend.

gaps.detail: Would give a crib for the whole exchange.
